title: 辰密 (Chenmi): 4 numeric telegrams of Huang Xing's circle, Tokyo <-> Shanghai, 3 June - 13 June 1916 (JACAR)

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the copies; the texts are not in Hsueh Chun-tu's edition of Huang Xing's 1916 drafts (黃興等電稿) nor found online.

transcription.source: JACAR scans; transcribed with Claude (first trials with Codex), every digit re-read blind by Brice Dudout
transcription.notes: Clear prefix 6591 1378 left out of the count.

system.summary: The Chinese telegraph code (明密 book) with its pages, columns and rows renumbered by hand for the 辰密 correspondent (S. Tomokiyo); equivalently key C92 as a formula (key.md).
system.notes: Digits written in kanji numerals in a grid, read in columns right to left; the first two groups are a clear prefix naming the code book. One key, one entry: split from targets/numeric1916, as its NOTES propose.

prior_solution.where: None known: not in Hsueh Chun-tu's edition of Huang Xing's 1916 drafts (nothing between 8 and 20 June), nor online (Wenmi, Juin 1916 article). 黃興集 and Li Yuanhong's correspondence not yet checked.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout read the digits on the JACAR scans (blind re-reading), proposed the reading order of the grids, chose leads and criteria; Claude wrote the solvers, tests and log, proposed hypotheses, readings and translations; Codex made early trials.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Forms read in columns right to left, four-digit groups; every digit re-read blind by Brice Dudout.
Rongmi and Gongmi keys failed; permuted-page + permuted tens/units model annealed on N13, N16, N26 (201 groups).

The page table found follows the countdown of numbers without a zero, then imposed; 劈 for 力 and 滠 for 灰, both from groups ending 9, gave the rule units 9 = 10; N05 (not in the search, no prefix) then reads through.

Contributor (Wenmi verify.py): the key reproduces every published raw text from the re-read digits; score far above 200 random keys of the same form and 200 digit shuffles. Rerun independently in targets/numeric1916 (20 Oct 2026).
S. Tomokiyo (Cryptiana): the 辰密 key is a 明密 code book with pages, columns and rows renumbered by hand; the contributor checked the exact factorisation over all group values (mingmi.py).
Readings and translations as on the Wenmi page; counted by Daniel's rule: 232 certain, 7 probable, 0 unresolved or illegible of 239.

outcome.method_basis: Key search scored with a telegraph-code language model, without cribs or plaintext; only the form dates served as checks (key.md, NOTES.md).
outcome.fraction_read_source: Daniel's rule on reading.md: 232 certain + 7 probable of 239 groups (0 unresolved).

gaps.item: 7 characters read as probable (one-digit variants or context)
gaps.detail: Marked {x} in reading.md; the decryption keeps the figure's own value.

credits.note: 辰密: digits re-read on the JACAR scans, key C92 recovered with Claude (Opus 5.5), readings, translations and context
the 辰密 key read as a renumbered 明密 code book (pages, columns and rows rewritten by hand), shown on a June 1916 edition of the 明密碼電報書; credited on the Wenmi page

texts.label: 辰密 (Chenmi), 4 telegrams, 3 June - 13 June 1916
texts.summary: Four telegrams from Tokyo to the Hunanese group's address in Shanghai (ヒツキン, 277 Avenue Joffre): Shandong and Bo Wenwei; the joint telegram to Li Yuanhong, Cen Chunxuan and the provinces; an elite division under Zhao Hengti for Li Yuanhong; 300 yuan for Jiang Fangzhen.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 4 Nov 2026 (Chinese, classical telegraphic): all four telegrams read straight through (Shandong offer to Bo Wenwei; the joint telegram to Li Yuanhong and Cen Chunxuan; an elite division under Zhao Hengti for Li; 300 yuan to Baili). 239 groups, 7 probable readings, none unresolved: read, grade A.
